## Author decisions and display order

This planning document translates the accepted REPORT-018 reader corpus, the current Nature Health manuscript, the V0 display precedent, and the author's display decisions into one ordered manuscript package. It does not refit a model, recalculate a result, or alter an accepted hypothesis output. Where the author requested a changed figure or table, the preview is labelled as an editorial assembly or a coordinated display repair rather than as an already accepted output.

<div class="selection-status">
<div class="selection-card"><strong>Main displays</strong>Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–3 follow the author-approved narrative order.</div>
<div class="selection-card"><strong>Supplementary person-level synthesis</strong>The requested synthesis table is shown as a Supplementary display with a separate FDR-correction column.</div>
<div class="selection-card"><strong>Supplementary principle</strong>Every scientific Descriptives display not used in the main paper is assigned to Supplementary Information, except the removed redundant near-eye profile and construction-only outputs.</div>
<div class="selection-card"><strong>Numbering rule</strong>The labels in this document are the proposed manuscript labels. Source-report numbers shown inside accepted previews are provenance only.</div>
</div>

<div class="local-table-scroll" role="region" aria-label="Proposed manuscript display order" tabindex="0">

| Proposed order | Display | Status | Disposition |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Figure 1. Study protocol, sites, collection windows, civil photoperiod, and daily near-eye exposure** | Accepted | Main |
| 2 | **Table 1. Participant and site characteristics** | Accepted short manuscript table | Main |
| 3 | **Table 2. Recommendation adherence by Brown et al. recommendation window and day type** | Editorial assembly from accepted rows | Main |
| 4 | **Figure 2. Multiscale daily pattern of near-eye melanopic EDI** | Accepted | Main |
| 5 | **Table 3. Personal light-exposure metrics and their geographic and photoperiod context** | `gt` assembly from accepted Descriptives and H01 rows | Main |
| 6 | **Figure 3. Activity category and local-clock pattern of near-eye melanopic EDI** | Accepted H04 revision 3 four-panel composite | Main |

</div>

The Brown participant profile, H01/H07 geographic composite, H03 light-source composite, and hourly H06 displays remain in Supplementary Information. H03 must keep study-site and light-source colours distinct. The accepted H04 revision 3 composite uses consistent panel sizes, printed values, and registry-based site colours.

## Main displays

### Figure 1. Study protocol, sites, collection windows, civil photoperiod, and daily near-eye exposure

<img class="display-image" src="../../artifacts/10_figures/descriptives/descriptive_overview.svg" alt="Five-panel overview of the eight-day protocol, sensor positions, nine country-coded sites, collection windows, civil photoperiod, and the pooled near-eye daily profile.">

<div class="caption-proposal">
<strong>Manuscript caption.</strong> Study protocol, sites, collection windows, civil photoperiod, and daily near-eye exposure. <strong>A</strong>, Eight-day field protocol and sensor positions. The wrist logger is shown as a protocol device but is not an exposure channel analysed in this manuscript. <strong>B</strong>, Nine sites in seven countries. <strong>C</strong>, Site collection periods. <strong>D</strong>, Observed civil photoperiod. <strong>E</strong>, Site and pooled 15-minute median near-eye melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance profiles from 816 participant-days contributed by 141 participants, repeated over 48 hours for display only. Grey ribbons show the central 50% and 90% of measured values, not confidence intervals; coloured lines are site medians, the black line is the pooled median, and red and blue shading show mean reported sleep and civil night. During reported sleep, the measurement represents the bedside sleep environment.
</div>

### Table 1. Participant and site characteristics

{{< include figure_table_selection_assets/tbl-participant-site-manuscript.html >}}

<div class="caption-proposal">
<strong>Manuscript caption.</strong> Participant and measurement characteristics overall and by country-coded study site. The table distinguishes the 191-person roster, participants and participant-days with recorded light data, and the screened near-eye and complementary chest samples. Near-eye, chest, and paired support are reported separately; model-specific samples are reported with each analysis. Of the 191 roster participants, 184 contributed the 1,478 recorded participant-days. Continuous participant characteristics are median with the stated percentile range.
</div>

### Table 2. Recommendation adherence by Brown et al. recommendation window and day type

{{< include figure_table_selection_assets/tbl-plan-brown-main-adherence.html >}}

<div class="caption-proposal">
<strong>Manuscript caption.</strong> Recommendation adherence by Brown et al. recommendation window and day type. Daytime, Pre-sleep, and Sleep identify the recommendation windows used for comparison. Daytime comprises diary-defined wake excluding the three hours before sleep, Pre-sleep comprises those three hours, and Sleep uses near-eye illuminance recorded during the reported sleep interval and does not describe the bedroom light environment. Pooled minutes meeting recommendation report the number and percentage of valid measured minutes whose exposure lay within the applicable range. Work-day and Free-day percentages, differences, 95% confidence intervals, and false-discovery-rate-adjusted p-values are site-average estimates from the main state-period model, with each of the nine sites weighted equally. The pooled-minute fractions and modelled state-period estimates are distinct estimands. The main model included 2,216 state periods from 140 participants and 782 behavioural cycles, representing 1,028,958 valid minutes. Adherence is defined at the measured-minute or state-period level and does not classify participants or estimate health risk.
</div>

### Figure 2. Multiscale daily pattern of near-eye melanopic EDI

<img class="display-image" src="../hypotheses/H02/report018_order72_svg_export/candidate/figure4_exact_layout_replication.svg" alt="Four-panel display of the site-average, site-specific, participant-specific, and site-to-average daily near-eye melanopic EDI patterns.">

<div class="caption-proposal">
<strong>Manuscript caption.</strong> Multiscale daily pattern of near-eye melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance. <strong>A</strong>, Site-average daily curve. <strong>B</strong>, Fitted site curves. <strong>C</strong>, Fitted participant curves after the shared local-clock and site patterns were considered. <strong>D</strong>, Ratio of each fitted site curve to the site-average curve on the melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance plus 0.1 lx scale. Grey bands show mean civil night. Shaded bands are clock-specific 95% confidence intervals; red segments identify displayed half-hours whose interval did not include the site-average curve and are descriptive clock-specific contrasts. The analysis included 141 participants and 816 participant-days across nine sites. If the accepted artwork retains “global time effect”, it denotes the site-average local-clock curve.
</div>

### Table 3. Personal light-exposure metrics and their geographic and photoperiod context

The preview combines accepted metric descriptions, overall near-eye distributions, accepted density thumbnails, accepted H01 site and civil-photoperiod evidence, participant-associated model information, and model-specific R² quantities. Latitude and site-versus-latitude adequacy remain in Supplementary Information.

{{< include figure_table_selection_assets/table3_gt_candidate_revision/tbl-plan-h01-metric-synthesis-candidate.html >}}

<div class="coordination-note">
<strong>Definition alignment.</strong> MDER uses the accepted mean of viable minute-level ratios in both the descriptive summary and the H01 model results.
</div>

<div class="caption-proposal">
<strong>Manuscript caption.</strong> Near-eye personal light-exposure metrics and their geographic and photoperiod context. Descriptive exposure values are median (interquartile range). Density plots show accepted site distributions and are descriptive. Metrics are grouped into thematic streams and describe distinct features of the daily exposure pattern rather than interchangeable health-response estimates. Model cells report overall-site evidence, civil-photoperiod associations with 95% confidence intervals, false-discovery-rate decisions, participant-associated model information, and model-specific R² summaries where applicable. Site and photoperiod part-R² values may contain overlapping fitted information and must not be summed. Associations are observational. Absolute latitude is fixed within and confounded with study site; complete latitude and model-adequacy results are reported in Supplementary Information.
</div>

### Figure 3. Activity category and local-clock pattern of near-eye melanopic EDI

<div class="manuscript-composite">
<img class="display-image" src="figure_table_selection_assets/H04_manuscript_figure3_selection_candidate.svg" alt="Four-panel display of fitted near-eye melanopic EDI, activity ratios, effective weighted support across local clock time, and activity-by-site estimates.">
</div>

<div class="coordination-note"><strong>Accepted selection candidate.</strong> H04 revision 3 passed independent non-circular verification and original-size and 170-mm visual QA. Panels A–D use uppercase left-edge tags, panel B uses the unclipped “Ratio to global mean” axis title, and panel D uses compact P/D/H support headers and borderless registry-coloured site markers. The table includes the accepted display-only Other row and marks all nine unsupported Other-by-site cells as Not estimable. Frozen scientific values and internal category keys remain unchanged.</div>

<div class="caption-proposal"><strong>Manuscript caption.</strong> Exploratory near-eye time-of-day patterns and site-specific activity context. Panels <strong>A</strong>, <strong>B</strong>, and <strong>C</strong> show site-average activity-associated melEDI by local time, ratios to the global cyclic smooth, and effective weighted support. Panel <strong>D</strong> shows site-average estimates and site-specific deviation ratios. The five named categories use the activity-by-site interaction model. Other is the accepted additive display-only estimate and is excluded from that interaction model. Parentheses contain 95% confidence intervals. Bold site ratios and FDR p-values pass the complete 44-member near-eye family. Unsupported activity-by-site cells, including all Other site cells, are not estimable. The five-category interaction frame comprises 126 participants, 724 participant-days, 16,135 unique participant-hours, 16,875 generated long rows, 16,135 effective weighted hours, nine sites, and 4,746 exact-zero participant-hours. Each multi-select participant-hour contributes 1/k across retained categories. Other-only display support comprises 72 participants, 159 participant-days, and 391 unique participant-hours. P denotes participants, D participant-days, and H unique participant-hours.</div>

### Recommendation adherence

The three Brown figures use the display order requested by the author. The axis contract is **Daytime, Pre-sleep, Sleep**. These are Brown et al. recommendation windows, not contexts. “Evening” is replaced by “Pre-sleep” only when it denotes the same three-hour window. “Context” remains available for genuine sensor-position or measurement qualifications.

#### Supplementary Figure S4. Site-average recommendation adherence

<img class="display-image" src="figure_table_selection_assets/brown_adherence_levels.svg" alt="Point-range chart of recommendation adherence for the Daytime, Pre-sleep, and Sleep Brown et al. recommendation windows. Blue circles show Work days and orange triangles show Free days; vertical bars show 95% confidence intervals. Daytime and Sleep adherence are lower on Free days, while Pre-sleep adherence is higher. The Sleep-window estimates are based on near-eye illuminance recorded during sleep, not bedroom environmental light.">

<div class="caption-proposal"><strong>Caption.</strong> Recommendation adherence in the Daytime, Pre-sleep, and Sleep recommendation windows on Work and Free days. Points are equal-site average percentages of valid minutes meeting the Brown et al. recommendation; bars are 95% confidence intervals. Daytime, Pre-sleep, and Sleep identify the three Brown et al. recommendation windows. The Sleep estimate uses near-eye illuminance recorded during sleep and does not describe the bedroom light environment.</div>

#### Supplementary Figure S5. Site-specific adherence and day-type differences

<img class="display-image" src="figure_table_selection_assets/brown_supplementary_figure_s5.svg" alt="Two-panel forest plot of site-specific Brown recommendation adherence. Panel A shows Work-day adherence for nine country-coded sites in each of the Daytime, Pre-sleep, and Sleep recommendation windows. Panel B shows Free-day minus Work-day differences for the same sites and windows. Every point has a 95% confidence interval, and long-dashed blue lines mark equally weighted site averages. Filled diamonds and black asterisks distinguish the prespecified false-discovery-rate decisions described in the caption.">

<div class="caption-proposal"><strong>Caption.</strong> Site-specific adherence to the Brown et al. recommendations. <strong>A</strong>, Modelled Work-day recommendation adherence for each site and Brown recommendation window. Points show site estimates and bars show 95% confidence intervals. The long-dashed blue line gives the equally weighted site-average estimate for each window. Filled diamonds identify stored site-minus-average contrasts that passed their prespecified false-discovery-rate threshold. <strong>B</strong>, Modelled Free-day minus Work-day differences. The dotted black line marks no difference, and the long-dashed blue line gives the equally weighted site-average difference for each window. Orange diamonds identify contrasts versus zero that passed their prespecified false-discovery-rate threshold. Black asterisks identify departures from the site-average difference that passed the separate prespecified threshold. The rows represent the Daytime, Pre-sleep, and Sleep recommendation windows defined by Brown et al.; Pre-sleep is the three hours before sleep. Sleep-window estimates describe recorded near-eye illuminance during sleep and should not be interpreted as the bedroom environment. All estimates come from pooled interaction models. Sites are not independent replications, and the figure does not estimate causal effects of location.</div>

#### Supplementary Table S4. Exploratory cross-window recommendation-adherence associations

{{< include figure_table_selection_assets/tbl-plan-brown-cross-window-associations.html >}}

<div class="caption-proposal"><strong>Caption.</strong> Exploratory within-participant and between-participant associations across Brown et al. recommendation windows. Results are percentage-point differences per 10 percentage points higher Daytime adherence. All four primary tests form one FDR-correction set. The within-participant day-level claim is withheld because serial dependence remains unresolved. Between-participant results describe observed monitoring-period averages and do not establish rankings, stable traits, or causal effects.</div>

#### Supplementary Figure S6. Anonymous participant recommendation-adherence profiles

<figure id="fig-s6" class="display-figure">

Colored points show anonymous participants' equal-cycle means, faint lines connect the same participant across windows, half-violin shapes show the window distributions, and dark bars with white points show interquartile ranges and medians. <figcaption><strong>Supplementary Figure S6.</strong> Participant-average recommendation adherence across the Brown et al. recommendation windows. Daytime, Pre-sleep, and Sleep are the window labels. Each colored point is one anonymous participant's equal-cycle mean within that window. Faint lines connect the same anonymous participant across the three window summaries; they are not time trajectories or ranks. Half-violin shapes show the window distributions, and dark bars with white points show interquartile ranges and medians. Because each window has its own Brown et al. threshold and direction, absolute percentages should be interpreted within window.</figcaption>

### Daily architecture

#### Supplementary Table S5. Near-eye fitted-curve dispersion and conditional Shapley allocation

{{< include figure_table_selection_assets/remaining_gt_candidates/tbl-plan-h02-glasses-variation-shapley-gt-candidate.html >}}

<div class="caption-proposal"><strong>Caption.</strong> Near-eye fitted-curve dispersion and conditional Shapley allocation of in-sample model fit. Fitted-curve variation is in squared log10(melanopic EDI + 0.1 lx) prediction units; curve and Shapley ratios are unitless. Conditional Shapley values allocate in-sample R², with the shared local-clock curve fitted as the mandatory baseline. Intervals are 95% percentile hierarchical cluster-bootstrap intervals from 2,000 replicates and are conditional on the fitted models. These quantities describe different estimands and should not be added or interpreted causally.</div>

### Geographic and civil-photoperiod context

#### Supplementary Figure S7. H01 support and H07 nonlinear classifications

<img class="display-image" src="figure_table_selection_assets/supplementary_figure_s6.svg" alt="Two-panel figure. Panel A is an FDR support matrix for site, civil photoperiod, latitude, and site-versus-latitude adequacy across four separate 17-metric families. Panel B shows near-eye response smooths and first derivatives across observed civil photoperiod.">

<div class="coordination-note"><strong>Accepted single composite.</strong> The H01 and H07 panels are embedded in one owner-sealed composite with uppercase left-side A/B tags. The accepted component images, equal displayed widths, top alignment, and scientific content are unchanged.</div>

<div class="caption-proposal"><strong>Caption.</strong> Geographic and civil-photoperiod associations across near-eye personal light-exposure metrics. <strong>A</strong>, Evidence retained after FDR adjustment for overall site, civil photoperiod, latitude, and site-versus-linear-latitude adequacy. <strong>B</strong>, Nonlinear civil-photoperiod associations and their fitted slopes. A qualifying transition denotes an increase followed by a sustained near-flat tail under the accepted derivative rule. These descriptive associations do not identify a mechanism, and no physiological or environmental ceiling was identified.</div>

## Cross-display language and construction contract

- Use **personal light exposure** for the broad construct, **near-eye sensor position** for the qualified wearable estimate, **complementary chest sensor position** for non-ocular placement evidence, and **bedside sleep environment** during reported sleep. Use **primary** only when needed to distinguish a prespecified analysis from a complementary or sensitivity analysis.
- For Brown displays, use **Daytime**, **Pre-sleep**, and **Sleep** as axis labels. Captions state that these are the Brown et al. recommendation windows. They are not called contexts. Replace **Evening** with **Pre-sleep** only when it denotes the exact three-hour pre-sleep window.
- Use **recommendation adherence** for the Brown outcome. Do not expose BA-M labels.
- Use **site-average estimate** when each site contributes equally and explain the equal weighting.
- Use **FDR**, never BH, in reader-facing displays. Confidence-interval exclusion and FDR decisions are separate evidence statements.
- Omit raw p-values from the H05, H08, H09, and H10 selected tables. Retain estimates, 95% confidence intervals, FDR-adjusted values or decisions, exact samples, and qualifications.
- Describe Shapley values as conditional in-sample model-fit credit, not response variance explained, causal importance, or a unique variance partition.
- Use **marginal R²**, **conditional R²**, **participant-associated share**, and **model-specific term part-R² values that may overlap and must not be summed**.
- Never pool near-eye and complementary chest evidence.
- Use association, contrast, difference, or ratio rather than causal-effect language.
- Every site name carries its country code.
- A non-retained result is inconclusive, not evidence of no association. Non-estimable cells remain explicit.

## Provenance and reproducibility

The table previews were generated by `scripts/report_harmonization/build_manuscript_figure_table_selection.R` under R 4.6.1. The builder checks each accepted source and HTML identity, extracts only selected reader endpoints, removes raw p-value columns or cell text only in the planning copies requested by the author, preserves FDR information, namespaces native `gt` semantics, and records source and artifact identities. It does not execute a hypothesis QMD or calculate a new result. Figure references and current numbering were reconciled under REPORT-018 Order 72e against the accepted 20-SVG manifest; the historical builder remains provenance for the unchanged table extraction and planning assets.
